Kim / Marcus — quick commercial view: Arcadia is strategic and mid-market procurement is pushing this. A hard requirement that attribution cannot be removed will make a lot of our customers nervous (they want control of UI/labels). But a compromise we could offer:

- Attribution suggestion: we provide a standard attribution snippet that Arcadia may surface; it is not required by downstream end-users. For co-branded flows (where Redwood models are central to the UX) we can require that partners notify end-users that third-party model outputs are used (privacy/FTC consistency), but not mandate an immutable tag in product code.

- Telemetry: accept an "opt-in training" Order Form line where Arcadia can check a box to allow their outputs to be used for model training with additional safeguards (anonymization + explicit consent). Otherwise, default is no output-based training. We should reserve the right to use aggregated/telemetry metrics for service quality unless it includes PII or customer-model outputs flagged Opt-Out.

Proposed attachment contains the short order form language (proposed_orderform_clause.txt). If legal is comfortable, I can present this to Arcadia procurement and show it's an enterprise-friendly compromise that doesn't give us free rein.

Eleanor — thanks for the clear redline and the procurement checklist. We discussed internally and have a proposed path forward below. Quoting your key asks at the top for context:

> "(1) Any Redwood-originated outputs embedded in our products carry a short attribution line that cannot be removed by Arcadia; (2) Telemetry may not be used for cross-customer training; Arcadia requests an opt-in order form mechanism for training telemetry."

Our proposed compromises (high level):

1) Attribution: we cannot agree to a clause that forces an immutable, non-removable tag in downstream product code. Instead we propose the following language for the MSA (snippet below) that balances Arcadia's transparency need and our customers' ability to control UX:

  - MSA §5.3 (proposed): "Customer may surface Model Outputs in Customer Products. When doing so, Customer shall adopt reasonable measures to disclose to end users that certain functionality is powered, in part, by third-party machine-generated content. Redwood may provide a suggested attribution snippet for Customer use; Customer retains control over presentation and may elect whether to include the suggestion in end-user UI."

2) Telemetry & Training: we agree to an Order Form opt-in for output-based training. Default is: Redwood may collect operational telemetry (latency, error rates, aggregated usage metrics) for service improvement; Customer Outputs will not be used for cross-customer model training unless Customer checks the Training Consent box on the Order Form. If consented, training will be subject to: (i) explicit annex documenting data flows; (ii) anonymization/sanitization measures; (iii) ability for Customer to revoke consent with a reasonable notice period.

Suggested Order Form line (to place under "Data & Training"):

  "Training Consent — Customer authorizes Redwood to use Customer Outputs for model training subject to the Training Annex (initially unchecked). If selected, the parties will execute the Training Annex describing scope, retention, and technical safeguards."

I've attached our suggested snippets in the redline we are returning (see attached). For transparency, Ben will present the commercial compromise to procurement, and Marcus will confirm the engineering telemetry boundaries. Laura has flagged two cleanup edits to the legalese which we will incorporate in the returned redline.

Can you confirm Arcadia can accept (A) the non-mandatory attribution wording and (B) the Order Form opt-in approach for training? If yes, we'll send a single consolidated redline by Friday EOD with tracked changes. If Arcadia absolutely requires an immutable, non-removable tag, please indicate the specific product contexts and business reasons so we can escalate internally.

Thanks — happy to set a 20 minute call tomorrow if that's faster.

Best,
